question: Can Cirrove's provider-neutral durable transfer and mutation workers safely replace and rename one exact Google Drive file by resolving an observed v3 version to a current v2 strong ETag immediately before mutation?
kind: Explicitly authorized, bounded live validation on one deterministic file previously created and retained by Cirrove's isolated Google write validator.
authorization: On 2026-09-20 the owner instructed Cirrove to plan and implement the Google writable path. Mutations are confined to the retained run-owned fixture and must restore its original name and deterministic bytes.
scope: The exact multipart file created by the completed Google create-validation run. The ordinary mounted Google account and every pre-existing user item are excluded.
arms: Repeat the already-passing direct v2 final-commit probe and restore the deterministic original file.
Read the restored file through the v3-version/v2-ETag bridge and replace its content through the provider-neutral durable TransferWorker.
Read back the exact item and SHA-256, then use its new version observation to restore the deterministic original bytes through the same worker.
Read the restored file through the version bridge, rename it through the provider-neutral MutationWorker, then use the new version to restore the original name.
Reuse the stale pre-rename version and require the mutation journal to reach Conflict before another write.
prediction: Both current version observations will resolve to a v2 strong ETag and commit through their shared workers; reusing the stale rename observation will conflict; exact name and bytes will be restored.
endpoint: Pass only if both worker operations reach their durable Applied/Uploaded state, exact-ID readback matches, the stale operation reaches Conflict, and the fixture is restored. Any uncertain, failed or accepted stale operation keeps normal Google mounts read-only.
known_limit: This probe uses raw provider names inside an isolated fixture. It does not resolve the mounted duplicate-safe name projection or Google's non-atomic duplicate-sibling collision rule.

corrections.outcome: The direct final-commit probe passed and restored the fixture. The provider-neutral worker then uploaded its deterministic replacement, but the credential required sign-in before the worker could restore the original bytes.
corrections.boundary: The test file contains the known 8 MiB + 47 byte 0x57 worker payload. The failed restore remains in the private journal; no other item was addressed.
corrections.correction: Reauthenticate the disabled validation account with the full Drive scope. Before a rerun, read the exact fixture by ID and version, require both the known replacement size and SHA-256, and only then restore the deterministic original through a newly journaled conditional worker operation. Refuse recovery for every other byte sequence.

corrections.outcome: Both provider-neutral content replacements completed and restored the original SHA-256. The first rename reached Applied. The immediate restoring rename crossed a v2/v3 consistency window, entered VerifyRequired and its first reconciliation reached Conflict.
corrections.boundary: The exact item and private journal are retained. A rerun may restore only the deterministic temporary name when the prior probe UUID and its Applied rename event match the current exact ID.
corrections.correction: Bound v3 confirmation of every v2 write response to five exact-ID reads separated by two seconds. Add synthetic lagging-v3 responses for content and metadata receipts. Before the rerun, conditionally restore a prior temporary name only when its UUID maps to retained matching evidence; refuse every other name.

corrections.outcome: The evidence-bound temporary name was restored, and the direct probe again passed. The first content worker then remained in VerifyRequired until the five-minute validator deadline; it did not retry the mutation.
corrections.boundary: The exact worker session and local snapshot remain journaled. A rerun applies the existing exact-size-and-SHA recovery gate before any new probe.
corrections.cause: Receipt confirmation had bounded v2/v3 settling, but reconciliation after an uncertain or expired resumable-session response still made only one v2/v3 comparison and one version-bound SHA read per worker pass.
corrections.correction: Apply the same bounded exact-ID v2/v3 settling to replacement reconciliation and retry the read-only SHA check after VersionChanged. Mutation is never retried during this loop.

corrections.outcome: Evidence-bound content recovery passed, the direct v2 probe passed, and both content-worker operations reached Uploaded. The following metadata operation became uncertain because Google advanced the general file version while the shared worker interpreted that value as a content revision.
corrections.cause: Drive file.version changes for metadata as well as content. It is suitable as the observation resolved to a write ETag, but not as the provider-neutral content lineage of a blob.
corrections.correction: Request v3 headRevisionId for binary files and publish it as google-revision:<id> for content identity while retaining google-version:<number> as the write precondition. Google documents headRevisionId as the head content revision for binary Drive files. Synthetic reads now accept a metadata version change with a stable head revision and still reject a changed head revision.

corrections.outcome: Stopped read-only before the direct probe because the current deterministic temporary name came from the prior operation whose journal had classified the result as Conflict rather than Applied.
corrections.correction: Permit name recovery when the prior evidence has the exact item, the exact UUID-encoded temporary name and a terminal Applied or Conflict result. In the Conflict case, the current exact remote name is the additional proof that the uncertain conditional rename committed; every unrelated name remains refused.

result.interpretation: The provider-neutral durable workers can replace and conditionally rename this app-created binary file through the v3-version/v2-ETag bridge. Binary headRevisionId supplies content lineage across metadata-only version changes. The duplicate-safe mounted name projection and non-atomic sibling collision rule remain open, so ordinary Google mounts stay read-only.
